solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Extremely crafty quintet brags about disreputable online activity (14)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.about: the letters are moved about, rearranged

blocks.note: the outer letters of CRAFTY
QUINTET BRAGS rearranged

annotation.surface: A crafty band of five boasts about their shady doings on the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: Cybersquatting is registering a web domain that matches someone else's name or brand, hoping to sell it to them.
annotation.definitionFit: Cybersquatting is grabbing domain names in bad faith, a disreputable thing to do online.

entries.clue: Token for trial demo (a responsive one) (14)

blocks.note: a counter is a token used in games
pro = for, in favour of
a test is a trial

annotation.surface: A token gesture laid on as a trial demonstration, one meant to answer something.
annotation.walkthrough: "Demo" is short for demonstration in the protest sense, not a trial product; the bracket narrows it to a protest made in reply to another.
annotation.definitionFit: A counterprotest is a demonstration staged in response to another one.

entries.clue: Airline finally can advance, having secured one place for aircraft (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: takes the final letter of each of the next two words
indicatorNotes.having secured: BA holds the new pieces inside it

blocks.note: BA = British Airways
I = one, the Roman numeral
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
the last letters of CAN and ADVANCE

annotation.surface: An airline pushing ahead at last after grabbing a slot for a plane.
annotation.walkthrough: "Finally" reaches past "can" to "advance" as well, taking the last letter of both. "Can advance" reads as a verb phrase, but neither word keeps its meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: A biplane is an aircraft with two pairs of wings.

entries.clue: Large grounds are located all in the middle of the country (5)

indicatorNotes.in the middle: takes the central letter of each word

blocks.note: five words, each of odd length, so each has a single central letter

annotation.surface: A description of a big estate sitting at the heart of the nation.
annotation.walkthrough: GROUNDS has seven letters, so its middle is U; each other word has an odd length with a single centre too.
annotation.definitionFit: Rural means of or belonging to the country rather than the town.

entries.clue: Financial wizard covering a doctor’s 25 per cent cut? (8)

indicatorNotes.covering: QUANT sits over A DR, around it

blocks.note: a quant is a quantitative analyst in finance
as printed
DR = doctor

annotation.surface: A money whizz demanding a quarter share of a doctor's earnings.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fee or commission; the definition is geometric, a quarter of a circle.
annotation.definitionFit: A quadrant is a quarter of a circle, a 25 per cent slice.

entries.clue: Reluctant explorers headed east (6)

indicatorNotes.headed: has its head, the first letter, removed

blocks.note: CAVERS, cave explorers, minus the C
E = east

annotation.surface: Some unwilling explorers set off towards the east.
annotation.walkthrough: "Headed east" reads as a direction of travel; here "headed" means beheaded, and "east" simply adds E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be averse to something is to be unwilling to do it.

entries.clue: Play electronic music, receiving cheer of approval (9)

blocks.note: trance is a genre of electronic dance music
olé, the Spanish cry of approval

annotation.surface: Someone playing a set of electronic music and getting cheers.
annotation.walkthrough: "Play" looks like a verb about the DJ; it is the noun, as in play in a steering wheel.
annotation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the permitted play or slack in a mechanism.

entries.clue: Type of salt regularly in oil and stock (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at a steady every-other spacing

blocks.note: the even letters of iN oIl
stock as in a stock phrase: trite, hackneyed

annotation.surface: Kitchen talk: a salt used regularly in oil and in a stock.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stock" looks like soup base in the cooking surface; it is the adjective meaning hackneyed.
annotation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a salt of nitrous acid, used for curing meat.

entries.clue: Seat assignment sent out as text? (7,7)

indicatorNotes.sent out: the letters are dispatched in a new order

blocks.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: An airline sending a passenger's seat allocation by text message.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that an instant message is an example of a text rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: An instant message is a short text sent and read in real time.

entries.clue: Feature of US drug lawsuit? (5,4)

blocks.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
a case is a lawsuit

annotation.surface: A drugs trial as a hallmark of American life.
annotation.walkthrough: "US" reads as the country; the definition means the two letters themselves, which are written as capitals.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: capital letters are one thing the abbreviation for the United States always has.

entries.clue: Admit to knowing head of local school (3,2)

indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its front end, its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of LOCAL
Eton is the famous English boarding school

annotation.surface: A local headteacher confessing to being in the know.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs "head" and "school" to suggest a headteacher, but "head of" only asks for one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To let on is to reveal or admit that you know something.

entries.clue: Follow Tesla alongside track (5)

blocks.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
a rail is a track

annotation.surface: Driving behind a Tesla car along a road next to a railway.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car brand; here it is the scientific unit, abbreviated T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: trailing a suspect means shadowing them from behind.

entries.clue: Control of retinue taken by others (9)

indicatorNotes.taken by: something taken by a person is held in their grasp, so the retinue ends up inside the others

blocks.note: the rest = the others
a train is a group of followers, a retinue

annotation.surface: Other people seizing command of a royal entourage.
annotation.walkthrough: "Retinue taken by others" puts the container second: the thing doing the taking is the outer word, even though it comes last in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: showing restraint means keeping yourself in check.

entries.clue: Wine periodically arrived with stronger, mixed drink (8)

blocks.note: the even letters of aRrIvEd
a sling is a mixed drink of spirits such as gin, stronger than wine

annotation.surface: Someone who turned up now and then, bringing a harder cocktail as well as wine.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mixed" looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the description of the drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white wine from the grape of that name.

entries.clue: Artist’s work wins top prize at the end (9)

indicatorNotes.at the end: takes the last letter of PRIZE

blocks.note: to land a prize is to win it
a cap is a top, as on a bottle
the last letter of PRIZE

annotation.surface: A painter's canvas taking first prize at the final judging.
annotation.walkthrough: "Top prize" reads as one phrase; "top" gives CAP and only the end of "prize" is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of scenery, an artist's work.

entries.clue: An academic from Quito, say (6)

blocks.note: as printed
a dean is a senior academic

annotation.surface: A university lecturer who comes from the capital of Ecuador.
annotation.walkthrough: Quito, the capital of Ecuador, lies high in the Andes; "say" marks it as one example of an Andean place.
annotation.definitionFit: Andean means from the Andes, where Quito stands.

entries.clue: Cats maybe cross over threshold? (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, turns the letters over, bottom to top

blocks.note: cats are an example of pets
a rood is a cross, a crucifix

annotation.surface: Cats wondering whether to cross the threshold into the house.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cross over" looks like one phrasal verb; "cross" is the noun ROOD and "over" turns everything round.
annotation.definitionFit: A doorstep is the step at a door, loosely its threshold.

entries.clue: Sport thriving from just after its inception (6)

indicatorNotes.from just after its inception: starts the word one letter after its beginning, dropping the first

blocks.note: growing = thriving

annotation.surface: A sport that flourished almost from the day it was founded.
annotation.walkthrough: The long phrase reads as history of the sport; it simply drops the G from GROWING.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: rowing is one sport among many, raced in boats with oars.

entries.clue: I’m enjoying this story — it may well be full of rubbish (7)

annotation.definition: it may well be full of rubbish

blocks.note: whee! is a cry of enjoyment
a story is a lie

annotation.surface: A reader loving a tale while admitting it is probably nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a wheelie, short for wheelie bin, is a wheeled household rubbish bin. "Full of rubbish" seems to judge the story, but it describes the bin.
annotation.definitionFit: A wheelie bin is where household rubbish goes.

entries.clue: Drive in second? Er … (8)

blocks.note: a second is a moment
um and er are both sounds of hesitation

annotation.surface: A learner driver asking whether to drive in second gear, then hesitating.
annotation.walkthrough: "Drive in second" suggests gears, but "in" is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a campaign with momentum has drive, the push that keeps it moving forward.

entries.clue: Visitor to Oz touring river close to city (7)

indicatorNotes.touring: TOTO travels round R and ON

blocks.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz
R = river
on = close to, as in a town on the coast

annotation.surface: A tourist in Australia going round a river near a city.
annotation.walkthrough: "Oz" reads as slang for Australia; the visitor is Dorothy's dog in the land of Oz.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Canada's largest city stands for cities in general.

entries.clue: Spirit of good admin worker broken by criticism (6)

indicatorNotes.broken by: G PA is split open with RAP between

blocks.note: G = good
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles
PA = personal assistant

annotation.surface: A good office assistant whose morale is crushed by criticism.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spirit" reads as morale; it is a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian spirit distilled from grape residue.

entries.clue: Money manager less hesitant after rate changes (9)

indicatorNotes.after: SURER is placed after the rearranged RATE

blocks.note: RATE rearranged
surer = more certain, less hesitant

annotation.surface: A fund manager growing more confident once interest rates move.
annotation.walkthrough: SURER comes first in the clue but last in the answer, because it sits after the jumbled RATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a club or charity hands its accounts and funds to the officer holding this post.

entries.clue: People working together in part of Apple broadcast? (5)

indicatorNotes.broadcast?: says it out loud, over the air

blocks.note: the core is the centre of an apple

annotation.surface: A team collaborating in a division of the tech company Apple, on the air.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital A pushes towards the company; the fruit is meant. CORPS is said "core", with silent P and S.
annotation.definitionFit: A corps is a body of people working together, like a press corps.

entries.clue: Smoke starts to intoxicate gamblers inside saloon, perhaps (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from each of the next two words
indicatorNotes.inside: what is inside something is enclosed by it, so these letters go within the car

blocks.note: a saloon is a type of car, a sedan
the first letters of INTOXICATE and GAMBLERS

annotation.surface: A Wild West scene: drunken gamblers puffing away in a saloon bar.
annotation.walkthrough: "Saloon" paints a Western bar; in British English it is a car body style, a sedan.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: "a smoke" is anything lit up and puffed, and a rolled tobacco leaf qualifies.

entries.clue: Series of coordinated steps featuring in appraisals, annoyingly (5)

indicatorNotes.featuring in: the answer appears inside the following words

blocks.note: the run starts near the end of the first word and crosses the comma into the second

annotation.surface: A tiresome step-by-step process that keeps turning up in staff reviews.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like office procedure; the steps are dance steps.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: any dance is a sequence of steps moved in time, and this Latin one is the example.

entries.clue: Father travelling again to region of South America (9)

indicatorNotes.travelling: things that are travelling change position, so the letters are on the move into a new order

blocks.note: pa = father
AGAIN TO rearranged

annotation.surface: Dad heading off once more to the far south of South America.
annotation.walkthrough: "Travelling again" reads as one idea; "travelling" is the only signal and "to" is part of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the land shared by Argentina and Chile at the continent's southern tip.

entries.clue: Open super-large complex useful for many things (7-7)

indicatorNotes.complex: the letters are tangled into a new arrangement

blocks.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A huge new complex opening its doors, built to serve many uses.
annotation.walkthrough: "Complex" reads as a noun, a building; it is the adjective telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Something general-purpose is useful for many different jobs.
